title: Car Fleet
description:
Cars start at distinct positions along a one-way road, all below a common destination target. The arrays position and speed describe the same cars by index. Return the number of separate fleets that reach the destination. A car cannot pass another car: when it catches a slower car or fleet, it joins it and continues at the slower speed.

Cars that reach the destination at the same moment count as one fleet even if they first meet exactly at the destination. A trailing car that would reach later on its own cannot join a faster group ahead. With no cars, return zero. Positions are unique, speeds are positive, and the input order is arbitrary.

The useful perspective is to sort from the car closest to the destination backward. Compare each car's solo arrival time against the fleet just ahead: if it would arrive sooner or at the same time, it must catch up. Otherwise it becomes a new fleet.

Example 1:

Input: target = 12, position = [10,8,0,5,3], speed = [2,4,1,1,3]
Output: 3

Example 2:

Input: target = 10, position = [3], speed = [3]
Output: 1

Example 3:

Input: target = 100, position = [0,2,4], speed = [4,2,1]
Output: 1

Constraints:

  • 0 <= position.length = speed.length <= 10,000.
  • 0 <= position[i] < target <= 1,000,000.
  • 1 <= speed[i] <= 1,000,000.
  • Starting positions are distinct.
